text: Now concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our being gathered to him, we ask you, brothers and sisters,
do not be quickly shaken in mind or alarmed—whether by a spirit, or a word, or a letter supposedly from us—claiming that the day of the Lord has already come.
Let no one deceive you in any way. That day will not come until the rebellion takes place and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction,
who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship, even seating himself in the temple of God, proclaiming himself to be God.
Don't you remember that I told you these things while I was still with you?
And you know what is now restraining him, so that he may be revealed at his proper time.
For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who restrains it is holding it back for now, until he is taken out of the way.

versions.text: For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who restrains it must first be taken out of the way.
versions.explanation: The Greek ἄρτι ("now") describes the restrainer as presently at work, and the clause with ἕως expresses continuation "until he is removed." The current rendering drops "now" and adds "first," turning a statement about ongoing restraint into a requirement of sequence.

versions.text: For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only there is one who restrains it now, until he is taken out of the way.
versions.explanation: The Greek clause is elliptical (μόνον ὁ κατέχων ἄρτι ἕως...), and the current rendering fills the gap with "only there is one who...", which stumbles when read aloud because "only" and "there is" collide. Making the restrainer the subject of a verb of restraining keeps both the adverb ἄρτι ("now") and the ἕως clause intact while giving a smoother oral rhythm.

text: Then the lawless one will be revealed, and the Lord Jesus will destroy him with the breath of his mouth and bring him to nothing by the splendor of his coming.
The coming of the lawless one is by the working of Satan, with all power and false signs and wonders,
and with every kind of wicked deception aimed at those who are perishing, because they refused to love the truth and so be saved.
For this reason God sends them a deluding power, so that they believe the lie,

versions.text: For this reason God sends them a powerful delusion, so that they believe the lie,
versions.explanation: ἐνέργειαν πλάνης is literally "a working/power of error." "A powerful delusion" shifts the noun-adjective relationship; "a deluding power" keeps the emphasis on the active working while reading just as smoothly aloud.

text: and so all who have not believed the truth but have delighted in wickedness will be condemned.

But we must always thank God for you, brothers and sisters loved by the Lord, because God chose you as the firstfruits for salvation, through the sanctifying work of the Spirit and faith in the truth.
To this he called you through our gospel, that you might obtain the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, brothers and sisters, stand firm and hold fast to the traditions you were taught, whether by our spoken word or by our letter.
Now may our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and by grace gave us eternal comfort and good hope,
comfort your hearts and strengthen you in every good work and word.
